name: Tiered bid management

rules.name: Scale proven winners
rules.reason: Converting below target ACoS with enough orders to trust the signal.

rules.name: Rein in hot but proven
rules.reason: The term converts, but above target. Reduce toward target rather than pausing.

rules.name: Warn - reduce before killing
rules.reason: Give the keyword a cheaper chance before switching it off.

rules.name: Kill
rules.reason: Enough spend to conclude the keyword does not convert.

notes: The field is actions, plural, and the action verb is the KEY. There is no type/mode/value triple: percent or dollars is chosen by the key itself, increase_bid_pct against increase_bid_dollar. One verb per rule.
Conditions within a rule are AND-ed.

max_bid is the ceiling a rule may never exceed, and it is set PER RULE inside that rule's actions. There is no automation-level max_bid. It is the primary safety property, more than undo is: a raising rule with no max_bid of its own runs against a $10.00 default, which is almost certainly not what you want.
Rule order is precedence. Where two rules would change the same bid, the earlier one wins, so the scaling rule sits above the cutting rules on purpose.
Metrics are SUMMED over lookback_days, not averaged. A longer window makes any threshold easier to trip. The maximum is 90 days.
campaign_ids takes Amazon campaign IDs, not campaign names, and at least one is required.
